lessons.description: Name brothers, sisters and spouses, and introduce people politely
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 姓 / 给你介绍一下

grammar.title: Asking a surname: 姓
grammar.note: 姓 (xìng) is a verb: 我姓王 = my surname is Wang. 您贵姓? (lit. 'your honorable surname?') is the polite way to ask. Answer with 我姓…, never 我贵姓 — 贵 is only used for the other person.

grammar.title: Introducing: 给 + person + 介绍一下
grammar.pattern: 我给你介绍一下，这是我哥哥。
grammar.note: 给 marks who receives the introduction. 一下 after a verb softens it: 'let me just introduce…'. Then use 这是… for each person.

grammar.title: Counting siblings: 有 + number + 个
grammar.pattern: 我有两个姐姐、一个弟弟。
grammar.note: Use 有 + number + 个 + family word. The list comma 、 separates items. 你家有几口人? asks how many people are in your family (口 is the measure word for household members).

sentences.en: What is your surname?
My surname is Li; my name is Li Ming.

sentences.zh: 我给大家介绍一下，这是我妻子。
sentences.en: Let me introduce to everyone — this is my wife.

sentences.zh: 我有一个哥哥和两个妹妹。
sentences.en: I have one older brother and two younger sisters.

sentences.zh: 那个男人是我姐姐的丈夫。
sentences.en: That man is my older sister's husband.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hello! What is your surname?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 我姓张。这是我的家人，我给你介绍一下。

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 这是我丈夫，那是我们的孩子。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.zh: 你们的孩子真漂亮！你有哥哥吗？
dialogue.en: Your child is really beautiful! Do you have an older brother?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 没有。我有一个姐姐和一个弟弟。
dialogue.en: No. I have one older sister and one younger brother.

lessons.description: Talk about your daily routine, hours and finished actions
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 已经…了 / 每…都 / 就

grammar.title: Already: 已经 + verb + 了
grammar.note: 已经 (yǐjīng) goes before the verb and 了 comes at the end. 他已经上班了 = He has already gone to work. To say 'not yet', use 还没 + verb: 我还没起床.

grammar.title: Every: 每 + measure + noun + 都
grammar.note: 每 = every. Add 都 before the verb to stress 'without exception'. 每天 (every day), 每个人 (everyone), 每次 (every time).

grammar.title: Duration: verb + time span
grammar.note: How long something lasts goes AFTER the verb: 睡了七个小时 (slept seven hours). Compare: a point in time (七点) goes BEFORE the verb.

grammar.title: Early: 就
grammar.note: 就 after a time word means 'as early as / already then'. 我六点就起床了 = I got up as early as six. It often pairs with 了.

sentences.zh: 我每天早上六点半起床。
sentences.en: I get up at 6:30 every morning.
What time do you go to work?

sentences.zh: 八点开始上课，我七点就到学校了。
sentences.en: Class starts at eight; I already got to school at seven.
I have already finished eating.

sentences.zh: 今天我很累，想休息一个小时。
sentences.en: I'm tired today and want to rest for an hour.

sentences.zh: 我哥哥在一个大公司上班。
sentences.en: My older brother works at a big company.

dialogue.en: What time do you get up every day?

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.en: One hour. I start work at eight.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.zh: 现在已经十点了，你还没休息吗？
dialogue.en: It's already ten now — you haven't rested yet?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Not yet, I haven't finished my work.

lessons.description: Talk about sports, how well people do things, and how often
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: verb + 得 + adj / number + 次

grammar.title: How well: verb + 得 + adjective
grammar.note: 得 (de) links a verb to a description of how it is done. 她唱得很好 = She sings well. If the verb has an object, repeat the verb: 他打篮球打得很好.

grammar.title: How often: verb + number + 次
grammar.note: 次 (cì) counts occurrences. 去过两次 = been twice. 第一次 = the first time. With a separable verb like 游泳, 次 can split it: 游三次泳.

grammar.title: Together: 一起 + verb
grammar.note: 一起 (yìqǐ) goes before the verb. 和…一起 = together with someone: 我和哥哥一起打篮球.

sentences.en: What sport do you like?
I really like playing basketball.
She dances very well.

sentences.zh: 我一个星期跑三次步，身体很好。
sentences.en: I run three times a week, and I'm very healthy.

sentences.zh: 周末我们一起去踢足球吧！
sentences.en: Let's go play football together this weekend!

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.en: How well do you swim?

dialogue.speaker: B

lessons.description: Say how you travel, how far places are, and from where to where
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: A 离 B 远/近 / 从…到…

grammar.title: Distance: A 离 B + 远/近
grammar.note: 离 (lí) measures distance between two places: A 离 B 很远 = A is far from B. Ask with 远吗? or 远不远? Don't use 从 here — 从 is for movement, 离 is for distance.

grammar.title: From … to …: 从 A 到 B
grammar.pattern: 从我家到机场要一个小时。
grammar.note: 从 marks the starting point, 到 the end. It works for places and times: 从八点到十二点 (from 8 to 12).

grammar.title: How you go: 坐 / 骑 + vehicle + 去
grammar.pattern: 我坐公共汽车去，他骑自行车去。
grammar.note: Ride inside (bus, train, boat, plane) = 坐. Ride on top (bicycle, horse) = 骑 (qí). On foot = 走路去. The vehicle comes before the verb of motion.

sentences.en: Is your home far from here?

sentences.zh: 不远，走路十分钟就到了。
sentences.en: Not far — it's ten minutes on foot.

lessons.description: Describe positions and directions; come in and go out
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 在…旁边 / 进来·出去 / 第 + number

grammar.title: Position: thing + 在 + place + 旁边/左边/右边
grammar.note: Place words come after the reference noun: 学校旁边 (next to the school), 门外 (outside the door). You can also flip it: 商店旁边是银行 = next to the store is the bank.

grammar.title: Direction: 进/出 + 来/去
grammar.note: 来 = toward the speaker, 去 = away from the speaker. If you're inside the room: 进来 (come in), 出去 (go out). If you're outside: 进去 (go in), 出来 (come out).

grammar.title: Ordinals: 第 + number
grammar.pattern: 第一个房间 / 第三天
grammar.note: Put 第 (dì) before any number to make it 'first, second…': 第一 (first), 第二 (second). Then add a measure word: 第一次 (the first time).

grammar.title: Towards: 向 + direction + verb
grammar.note: 向 (xiàng) = towards. 向前走 = walk forward. 向左 / 向右 = to the left / right. Common for giving directions.

sentences.zh: 我的房间在左边，哥哥的在右边。
sentences.en: My room is on the left; my brother's is on the right.

lessons.description: Order food and drinks, make suggestions and say what tastes good
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: …吧 / 要 + noun / 好 + verb

grammar.title: Suggestions: …吧
grammar.note: 吧 (ba) at the end turns a statement into a soft suggestion: 'let's…'. 走吧! = Let's go! It can also mean 'I suppose…?': 你是老师吧? = You're a teacher, right?

grammar.title: Ordering: 要 + amount + food
grammar.pattern: 我要一杯咖啡和两个鸡蛋。
grammar.note: 要 (yào) = to want / to order. 你要什么? = What would you like? Add 来 for a casual order: 来一碗米饭 = 'bring a bowl of rice'.

grammar.title: Good to …: 好 + verb
grammar.pattern: 好吃 / 好喝 / 好看
grammar.note: 好 before a sense verb makes an adjective: 好吃 (tasty), 好喝 (nice to drink), 好看 (good-looking), 好玩 (fun). Negative: 不好吃.

sentences.en: Welcome! Please sit down.
Waiter, we'd like to order.
The lamb here is really delicious.

lessons.description: Handle prices in hundreds and thousands, bargain and buy gifts
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 多少钱一公斤 / 别 + verb / 给 + person

grammar.title: Price per unit: 多少钱一 + measure
grammar.pattern: 苹果多少钱一公斤？— 十元一公斤。
grammar.note: Chinese puts the price first and the unit second: 十块一公斤 = ten kuai per kilo. 元 (yuán) is the written unit; in speech people say 块 (kuài).

grammar.title: Big numbers: 百 and 千
grammar.note: 百 = hundred, 千 = thousand. Use 两 instead of 二 before 百 and 千: 两百, 两千. A zero in the middle is spoken: 一百零五 (105).

grammar.title: Don't: 别 + verb
grammar.note: 别 (bié) = don't. It's softer and more common in speech than 不要. 别客气 = you're welcome / don't be polite.

grammar.title: For someone: 给 + person + verb
grammar.pattern: 我给妈妈买了一个手表。
grammar.note: 给 before a person means 'for / to'. 送给 = give as a gift: 这是我送给你的. 给 can also be the main verb: 给我 = give me.

sentences.en: How much is watermelon per kilo?
This watch is 1,200 yuan.

questions.question: 苹果多少钱一公斤？
questions.questionEn: How much are apples per kilo?

questions.question: 这个商店的水果很贵。

lines.zh: 明天是爸爸的生日，我想给他买一个手表。

lines.zh: 妈妈说：别告诉爸爸，明天送给他！
lines.en: Mom said: don't tell Dad — give it to him tomorrow!

questions.question: 第二个手表多少钱？
questions.questionEn: How much was the second watch?

questions.question: 妈妈让"我"今天告诉爸爸。
questions.questionEn: Mom told the narrator to tell Dad today.

lessons.description: Describe the weather, give opinions, guess and hope
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 觉得 / 可能 / 希望

grammar.title: Opinion: 觉得 + clause
grammar.note: 觉得 (juéde) = to feel / to think. It introduces a whole sentence: 我觉得这本书很好. Ask someone's view: 你觉得怎么样?

grammar.title: Maybe: 可能 + verb
grammar.note: 可能 (kěnéng) before the verb = maybe / probably. 他可能不来 = He might not come. 可能 can also stand alone as 'possible': 不可能! = Impossible!

grammar.title: Hope: 希望 + clause
grammar.note: 希望 (xīwàng) takes a full sentence after it, like 觉得. 希望你快乐 = I hope you're happy.

grammar.title: Soon: 快…了
grammar.note: 快 + verb/adj + 了 = 'about to…'. 快八点了 = It's almost eight. 天快黑了 = It's getting dark. Also: 要…了 means the same.

sentences.en: It's sunny today — the weather is really nice!
It's clouded over; it's about to rain.

sentences.zh: 我觉得北京的冬天很冷。
sentences.en: I think Beijing's winter is very cold.
It might snow tomorrow.
I hope it doesn't rain this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What's the weather like today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 早上是晴天，下午可能会阴。
dialogue.en: Sunny this morning; it may cloud over this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do you think it'll rain?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It might. Take an umbrella.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I really hope it snows tomorrow!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Impossible — it's June!

lines.zh: 昨天天很阴，非常冷。
lines.en: Yesterday was overcast and very cold.

lines.zh: 妈妈说：今天晚上可能下雪。
lines.en: Mom said: it might snow tonight.

lines.zh: 早上起床，外边都是白色的！
lines.en: When I got up this morning, everything outside was white!

lines.zh: 我觉得下雪的时候真漂亮。
lines.en: I think it's really beautiful when it snows.

questions.question: 昨天天气怎么样？
questions.questionEn: What was the weather like yesterday?

questions.question: 早上外边下雪了。
questions.questionEn: This morning there was snow outside.

lines.zh: 快下雨了，我们走快一点儿吧。
lines.en: It's about to rain — let's walk faster.

lines.zh: 路上人很多，车开得很慢。
lines.en: The road is crowded and cars are moving slowly.

lines.zh: 雨天开车要慢一点儿。
lines.en: On rainy days you should drive more slowly.

lines.zh: 我希望明天是晴天。
lines.en: I hope tomorrow will be sunny.

questions.question: 车开得很快。
questions.questionEn: The cars are going fast.

questions.question: "我"希望明天怎么样？
questions.questionEn: What does the narrator hope for tomorrow?

lessons.description: Say what's wrong, give reasons, and follow advice
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 因为…所以… / 让 + person + verb

grammar.title: Cause and effect: 因为…，所以…
grammar.pattern: 因为我生病了，所以没去上班。
grammar.note: 因为 (because) introduces the reason, 所以 (so) the result. Unlike English, Chinese happily uses both in one sentence. Either half can also stand alone.

grammar.title: Make / let someone: 让 + person + verb
grammar.note: 让 (ràng) = to let / to tell someone to do something. 妈妈让我早点儿睡觉 = Mom told me to sleep early. 让我看看 = Let me see.

grammar.title: Tell: 告诉 + person + information
grammar.pattern: 请告诉我你的电话号码。
grammar.note: 告诉 (gàosu) takes the person first, then what you tell them. 他告诉我他生病了 = He told me he was sick. Don't use 说 with a person object this way.

grammar.title: Why: 为什么
grammar.note: 为什么 (wèishénme) goes before the verb, after the subject. Answer with 因为… 为 (wèi) alone means 'for (the sake of)': 为你高兴 = happy for you.

sentences.en: What's wrong? Where does it hurt?
I'm sick, and my eyes hurt.

sentences.zh: 医生让我每天吃三次药。
sentences.en: The doctor told me to take medicine three times a day.

sentences.zh: 因为太累了，所以他今天没去上班。
sentences.en: Because he was too tired, he didn't go to work today.
Why didn't you tell me?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.zh: 你今天为什么没来上课？
dialogue.en: Why didn't you come to class today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 因为我生病了，所以去医院了。
dialogue.en: Because I got sick, so I went to the hospital.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What did the doctor say?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 医生说我太累了，让我多休息。
dialogue.en: The doctor said I'm too tired and told me to rest more.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Do you need to take medicine?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 要，每天两次。明天我告诉老师。
dialogue.en: Yes, twice a day. I'll tell the teacher tomorrow.

lines.zh: 我每天看手机看很长时间。
lines.en: I look at my phone for a long time every day.

lines.zh: 昨天我的眼睛很不舒服。
lines.en: Yesterday my eyes felt really uncomfortable.

lines.zh: 医生告诉我：因为你看手机太多，所以眼睛累了。
lines.en: The doctor told me: because you look at your phone too much, your eyes are tired.

lines.zh: 医生让我少看手机，多休息。
lines.en: The doctor told me to look at my phone less and rest more.

questions.question: "我"为什么眼睛不舒服？
questions.questionEn: Why are the narrator's eyes uncomfortable?

questions.question: 医生让"我"多看手机。
questions.questionEn: The doctor told the narrator to use the phone more.

lines.zh: 我哥哥工作非常忙，每天都很累。
lines.en: My older brother is very busy at work and tired every day.

lines.zh: 上个星期他生病了。
lines.en: Last week he got sick.

lines.zh: 他吃了药，在家休息了三天。
lines.en: He took medicine and rested at home for three days.

lines.zh: 妈妈告诉他：身体最重要！
lines.en: Mom told him: your health is the most important thing!

questions.question: 哥哥在家休息了几天？
questions.questionEn: How many days did the brother rest at home?

questions.question: 哥哥工作不忙。
questions.questionEn: The brother isn't busy at work.

lessons.description: Talk about classes and tests; say whether you understood or got it right
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: verb + 懂/完/错 / 可以 / 什么意思

grammar.title: Result complements: verb + 懂 / 完 / 错 / 好
grammar.pattern: 我听懂了。/ 这个题我做错了。
grammar.note: A second verb or adjective after the main verb shows the result: 看懂 (read and understand), 做完 (finish doing), 写错 (write wrongly), 准备好 (get fully ready). Negate with 没: 我没听懂.

grammar.title: What does … mean: …是什么意思？
grammar.note: 意思 (yìsi) = meaning. 我不懂你的意思 = I don't get what you mean. Useful phrase: 不好意思 = sorry / excuse me (embarrassed).

grammar.title: Permission: 可以 + verb
grammar.pattern: 老师，我可以问一个问题吗？
grammar.note: 可以 (kěyǐ) = may / can (allowed). Answer yes with 可以, no with 不可以 or 不行. For skills learned, use 会 instead: 我会说中文.

sentences.zh: 明天有考试，我要好好准备。
sentences.en: There's an exam tomorrow; I need to prepare well.

sentences.zh: 老师，我没听懂，可以再说一次吗？
sentences.en: Teacher, I didn't understand — can you say it again?
I got the third question wrong.
What does this word mean?
Thank you for your help!

sentences.zh: 我不知道这个问题怎么回答，我去问老师。
sentences.en: I don't know how to answer this question; I'll go ask the teacher.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you ready for the exam?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 还没有。很多题我看不懂。
dialogue.en: Not yet. I can't understand a lot of the questions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.zh: 哪个问题？我可以帮助你。
dialogue.en: Which question? I can help you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: What does this sentence mean?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Look — answer it like this and it's correct.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I get it! Thanks so much.

lines.zh: 我们每个星期有三次汉语课。
lines.en: We have Chinese class three times a week.

lines.zh: 老师问问题，我们回答。
lines.en: The teacher asks questions and we answer.

lines.zh: 我听不懂的时候，就问老师。
lines.en: When I don't understand, I ask the teacher.

lines.zh: 现在我可以看懂中文报纸了！
lines.en: Now I can read Chinese newspapers!

questions.question: 他们一个星期有几次汉语课？
questions.questionEn: How many Chinese classes do they have a week?

questions.question: "我"现在可以看懂中文报纸。
questions.questionEn: The narrator can now read Chinese newspapers.

lines.zh: 今天的考试有二十个题。
lines.en: Today's exam had twenty questions.

lines.zh: 我用了一个小时就做完了。
lines.en: I finished it in just one hour.

lines.zh: 可是我做错了两个题。
lines.en: But I got two questions wrong.

lines.zh: 下次我要准备得更好。
lines.en: Next time I'll prepare better.

questions.question: "我"做错了几个题？
questions.questionEn: How many questions did the narrator get wrong?

questions.question: 考试有二十个题。
questions.questionEn: The exam had twenty questions.

lessons.description: Describe what people are doing right now and how things are
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: 正在…呢 / verb + 着

grammar.title: In progress: (正)在 + verb + (呢)
grammar.note: 正在 (zhèngzài) before a verb = 'right now, in the middle of'. 呢 at the end adds a friendly tone. Shorter forms: 在 + verb, or just verb + 呢. Negate with 没在: 我没在看电视.

grammar.title: Ongoing state: verb + 着
grammar.note: 着 (zhe) shows a lasting state: 门开着 (the door is open), 他穿着红衣服 (he's wearing red). Verb1 + 着 + verb2 = do verb2 while verb1: 笑着说 (say with a smile).

grammar.title: Wishes: 祝 + person + wish
grammar.note: 祝 (zhù) = to wish. 祝你身体好 (wishing you good health), 祝你考试好 (good luck on your exam).

sentences.en: Today is my birthday!
Happy birthday to you!
Mom is making a cake right now.
She said with a smile: thank you, everyone!

sentences.zh: 你给我打电话的时候，我正在开会。
sentences.en: When you called me, I was in a meeting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hello, what are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 我正在准备晚饭。有什么事情吗？
dialogue.en: I'm preparing dinner. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.zh: 明天是小王的生日，我们一起去吧！
dialogue.en: Tomorrow is Xiao Wang's birthday — let's go together!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Great! What are you giving her?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I want to give her a phone.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: She'll definitely be happy!

lines.zh: 今天是我妹妹的生日。
lines.en: Today is my younger sister's birthday.

lines.zh: 爸爸正在做饭，妈妈正在买蛋糕。
lines.en: Dad is cooking and Mom is buying a cake.

lines.zh: 我送给妹妹一本书。
lines.en: I gave my sister a book.

lines.zh: 她笑着说：谢谢哥哥！
lines.en: She said with a smile: thanks, big brother!

questions.question: 妈妈正在做什么？
questions.questionEn: What is Mom doing?

questions.question: "我"送给妹妹一个手机。

lines.zh: 晚上七点，朋友们都来了。
lines.en: At seven in the evening, all the friends arrived.

lines.zh: 大家一起唱歌，一起吃蛋糕。
lines.en: Everyone sang together and ate cake together.

lines.zh: 小李一直在看手机，他正在等女朋友的电话。
lines.en: Xiao Li kept looking at his phone; he was waiting for his girlfriend's call.

lines.zh: 这是我最快乐的一个生日！
lines.en: This was my happiest birthday ever!

questions.question: 小李为什么一直看手机？
questions.questionEn: Why did Xiao Li keep looking at his phone?

questions.question: 朋友们晚上七点来了。
questions.questionEn: The friends came at 7 p.m.

lessons.description: Share travel experiences, contrast ideas, and review all of HSK 2
lessons.grammarLabel: Pattern: verb + 过 / 虽然…但是… / 还

grammar.title: Experience: verb + 过
grammar.pattern: 我去过北京。/ 我没吃过羊肉。
grammar.note: 过 (guo) after a verb = 'have ever done'. It talks about experience, not one specific time. Negate with 没 + verb + 过. Ask: 你去过…吗? or 你去没去过…?

grammar.title: Although … but …: 虽然…，但是…
grammar.note: 虽然 (suīrán) introduces a concession, 但是 (dànshì) the contrast. Like 因为…所以…, Chinese uses both halves together — English drops one of them.

grammar.title: Still / also: 还
grammar.pattern: 我还想去上海。/ 他还没来。
grammar.note: 还 (hái) = still, also, in addition. 还有 = there's also. 还没 + verb = not yet. 还是 in a question = or: 你喝茶还是咖啡?

grammar.title: Comparison review: A 比 B + adj (+ amount)
grammar.note: From Lesson 12: A 比 B + adj. Add 多了 or 一点儿 after the adjective to say 'much' or 'a bit': 今天比昨天冷一点儿. Never put 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence.

sentences.en: Have you ever been to China?

sentences.zh: 去年我和家人去上海旅游了。
sentences.en: Last year my family and I travelled to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 我们住的宾馆离机场很近。
sentences.en: The hotel we stayed at was close to the airport.

sentences.zh: 虽然路很长，但是我们玩得很高兴。
sentences.en: Although the journey was long, we had a great time.

sentences.zh: 坐飞机比坐火车快多了。
sentences.en: Flying is much faster than taking the train.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Have you been to Beijing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 去过两次。去年还去了一次。
dialogue.en: Twice. I went again last year.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How is Beijing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 虽然冬天很冷，但是非常漂亮。
dialogue.en: Although the winter is cold, it's very beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.zh: 我还没去过，明年想去旅游。
dialogue.en: I haven't been yet; I want to travel there next year.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.zh: 好啊！我可以告诉你住哪个宾馆。
dialogue.en: Great! I can tell you which hotel to stay at.

lines.zh: 去年夏天，我和朋友去北京旅游了。
lines.en: Last summer, my friend and I travelled to Beijing.

lines.zh: 我们坐了十个小时的火车。
lines.en: We took a ten-hour train ride.

lines.zh: 虽然路很长，但是我们一点儿也不累。
lines.en: Although the trip was long, we weren't tired at all.

lines.zh: 我们住的宾馆很便宜，房间也很大。
lines.en: Our hotel was cheap and the room was big too.

lines.zh: 那是我第一次去北京，我还想再去！
lines.en: That was my first time in Beijing — I want to go again!

questions.question: 他们怎么去北京？
questions.questionEn: How did they get to Beijing?

questions.question: 宾馆很贵。
questions.questionEn: The hotel was expensive.

lines.zh: 我去过很多地方，可是没去过上海。
lines.en: I've been to many places, but never Shanghai.

lines.zh: 我朋友说上海比北京热。
lines.en: My friend says Shanghai is hotter than Beijing.

lines.zh: 她还说上海的鱼非常好吃。
lines.en: She also says the fish in Shanghai is delicious.

lines.zh: 我希望明年可以去上海看看。
lines.en: I hope I can go and see Shanghai next year.

questions.question: "我"去过上海。
questions.questionEn: The narrator has been to Shanghai.

questions.question: 朋友说上海怎么样？
questions.questionEn: What does the friend say about Shanghai?
